title: Small transformation task
business_scenario: Meeting notes must be rewritten into a fixed, concise format. No private knowledge is required, and output structure matters.
business_outcome: Produce concise, consistently structured meeting summaries with minimal implementation overhead.
knowledge_source: Meeting notes supplied in the request
knowledge_freshness: Per-request; no retained knowledge is needed
data_availability: Input notes are available; no reviewed training set is required initially
privacy_security: Meeting notes may be sensitive and must follow normal input-handling controls
latency_cost_constraints: Prefer low complexity and low cost
why_this_approach: A focused prompt plus structured output schema directly addresses transformation and formatting. Deterministic schema validation can reject malformed output.
rejected_alternative_reason: Training is premature until a prompt-and-schema baseline has been measured and shown inadequate.
key_risk: The model may omit fields or vary wording despite the prompt.
discovery_question: What exact fields and quality thresholds define an acceptable summary?
validation_plan: Evaluate representative meeting notes for schema validity, completeness, concision, latency, and cost.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: Volume may become high enough that tuning has a measured cost benefit
Deterministic extraction may be sufficient for highly regular notes

title: Changing internal policies
business_scenario: Employees ask questions about hundreds of internal policies that change regularly. Answers need source traceability.
business_outcome: Answer policy questions from current approved documents with traceable sources.
data_availability: Hundreds of source policies are available for indexing
privacy_security: Private documents require access control and retrieval filtering
latency_cost_constraints: Interactive latency with controlled retrieval and generation cost
why_this_approach: RAG retrieves current approved passages at request time and preserves evidence for citations without encoding changing policy content in model weights.
rejected_alternative_reason: Policy changes would trigger repeated tuning and tuned weights would not inherently provide reliable citations.
key_risk: Retrieval may miss the governing passage or expose content the user cannot access.
discovery_question: What repository, approval state, and user permissions determine which policy passages are retrievable?
validation_plan: Build a labelled policy QA set and measure corpus coverage, retrieval recall, grounded answers, citation validity, permissions, latency, and abstention.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: A tiny stable policy set might fit safely in prompt context
Some deterministic policy decisions may require rules rather than generation

title: Consistent specialized output behavior
business_scenario: A high-volume workflow needs specialized domain-specific format and behavior. Prompting has been tested extensively but remains inconsistent. A large set of reviewed input-output examples is available.
business_outcome: Improve consistent specialized behavior at production volume while preserving measurable quality.
knowledge_source: Reviewed input-output examples and request-time inputs
knowledge_freshness: Behavior is expected to remain stable; factual knowledge is not the tuning target
data_availability: Large reviewed and representative example set is available
privacy_security: Training examples require provenance, consent, sensitive-data review, and retention controls
latency_cost_constraints: High volume makes prompt length, latency, and operating cost important
why_this_approach: Fine-tuning is a testable candidate for persistent format and behavioral consistency after prompting has demonstrably failed. Constrained schemas and deterministic post-processing may still be required.
rejected_alternative_reason: Endlessly expanding a prompt ignores the measured inconsistency and may worsen token cost and latency.
key_risk: Poor or unrepresentative examples can teach inconsistent behavior and cause regressions.
discovery_question: Does a held-out evaluation show that fine-tuning materially beats the best prompt baseline on quality, latency, and cost?
validation_plan: Create train/validation/test splits, compare against the frozen prompt baseline, test schema validity and domain behavior, and run regression and safety checks.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: Constrained decoding or post-processing might solve the remaining inconsistency
The reviewed dataset may not represent production traffic

title: Current product information
business_scenario: A support assistant must answer from frequently updated product manuals and release notes, with citations.
business_outcome: Provide support answers tied to current product documentation and releases.
privacy_security: Respect product visibility, embargoes, and customer entitlements
why_this_approach: RAG can retrieve current versioned passages and cite them, while documents can be updated independently of the model.
rejected_alternative_reason: Embedding manuals in model weights creates freshness and traceability problems.
key_risk: Retrieval may mix product versions or rank obsolete notes above current guidance.
discovery_question: Must answers be filtered by product version, customer entitlement, or release channel?
validation_plan: Evaluate version-aware retrieval, citation mapping, stale-document exclusion, answer grounding, and update propagation time.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: One tiny stable manual could use prompt context
Deterministic lookup may handle exact compatibility tables

title: Deterministic eligibility rule
business_scenario: Eligibility is defined by a small set of explicit business rules, and every decision must be exactly reproducible and auditable.
business_outcome: Produce exact, reproducible eligibility decisions with a complete audit trail.
knowledge_source: Versioned explicit business rules and validated input fields
citation_requirement: Rule version and audit trace are required; generative citations are unnecessary
data_availability: Rules and decision inputs are explicitly defined
privacy_security: Protect decision inputs and audit logs
why_this_approach: Versioned deterministic code can produce the same output for the same inputs and record every rule applied.
rejected_alternative_reason: An LLM interpreting natural-language rules cannot guarantee exact reproducibility.
key_risk: Incorrect rule implementation or weak change control could produce systematically wrong decisions.
discovery_question: Are any eligibility criteria genuinely ambiguous, or can every condition be represented as validated inputs and rules?
validation_plan: Use decision tables, boundary tests, rule-version regression tests, audit-log checks, and independent business-owner approval.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: An LLM may assist with explanations but must not make the eligibility decision
Unstructured inputs may need a separately validated extraction step

title: Private knowledge plus specialized behavior
business_scenario: The assistant needs current internal knowledge with citations and must consistently follow specialized response behavior that prompting alone has not achieved reliably. High-quality training examples may be available.
business_outcome: Deliver current, cited internal answers in a reliable specialized response style.
knowledge_source: Current access-controlled internal documents plus reviewed behavior examples
knowledge_freshness: Internal knowledge changes; desired behavior is comparatively stable
data_availability: Documents exist; training examples must be verified before tuning
privacy_security: Document retrieval and any training data require access, provenance, sensitive-data, and retention controls
latency_cost_constraints: Combined retrieval and generation must meet measured service targets
why_this_approach: RAG owns current knowledge and citations. Fine-tuning is considered only for stable behavior after the RAG baseline proves prompting is insufficient.
rejected_alternative_reason: Fine-tuning alone is a poor primary store for changing private knowledge and does not inherently produce citations.
key_risk: The tuned behavior may override evidence-grounding rules or the training data may leak sensitive information.
discovery_question: Which failures remain after a measured RAG-and-prompt baseline, and are reviewed examples representative of those failures?
validation_plan: Compare a frozen RAG baseline with the combined system on retrieval, grounding, citation validity, behavior consistency, privacy, latency, cost, and regressions.
staged_approach: Establish and evaluate a RAG baseline
Compare combined system against the frozen baseline before release
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: RAG plus constrained prompting may already meet the behavior target
Insufficient reviewed examples would make tuning unjustified

title: Tiny known context
business_scenario: A user asks questions about one short policy that can be safely included directly in the request and changes rarely.
business_outcome: Answer from one short policy with minimal infrastructure and appropriate abstention.
knowledge_source: One short policy supplied directly in context
citation_requirement: Can reference the directly supplied policy; full retrieval traceability is unnecessary
privacy_security: Policy is approved for inclusion in the request
why_this_approach: Supplying the full short policy avoids retrieval complexity while keeping the answer grounded in visible context.
rejected_alternative_reason: A vector index adds complexity before document volume, context size, or freshness requires retrieval.
key_risk: The model may answer beyond the supplied policy instead of abstaining.
discovery_question: Will the policy set or document length grow beyond the safe context budget?
validation_plan: Test supported and unsupported questions, exact policy conditions, output schema, abstention behavior, latency, and token cost.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: Growth in document volume or update frequency could justify RAG
Exact rules may be better implemented deterministically

title: Missing discovery information
business_scenario: A stakeholder says, "We want to fine-tune our company data so ChatGPT knows everything internally."
business_outcome: Clarify the real business outcome and constraints before choosing an architecture.
data_availability: Reviewed training examples and source-document availability are unknown
privacy_security: Access control, retention, residency, and sensitivity are unknown
latency_cost_constraints: Accuracy, latency, scale, and cost targets are unknown
why_this_approach: Selecting fine-tuning before discovery confuses changing knowledge with persistent behavior. Essential requirements must be resolved first.
rejected_alternative_reason: There is no evidence that training data exists or that changing model behavior is the actual need.
key_risk: A premature architecture could expose private data, become stale, and fail the unstated business goal.
discovery_question: What business outcome is required; is the goal knowledge or behavior; how often does information change; are citations, deterministic results, access controls, reviewed examples, and specific accuracy, latency, and cost targets required; and what baseline has been tested?
validation_plan: Complete discovery, define measurable acceptance criteria, inventory approved data, establish the simplest baseline, then compare only architectures that satisfy the resolved requirements.
assumptions_that_could_change_decision: Changing cited knowledge would favor RAG
Persistent behavior with reviewed examples may favor fine-tuning
Explicit reproducible rules may require no LLM
